data.navTitle: 窗边叶片、绿色色样与说明图
data.title: Two leaves against the light

memoryNodes.cue: Maya compares a shade of green.
Arrows connect water, air and light.

data.situation:
Ruth held two fallen leaves against the light. They were different shades of green. A diagram beside the window described photosynthesis: green plants use light energy to make sugars from water and carbon dioxide. Their roots absorb water, while leaves take in carbon dioxide from the air. Chlorophyll helps capture light. Jo followed the arrows from the air to the leaf and then to the little sugar symbol; it was easier than reading the label from top to bottom. Jo: Does the diagram say the leaf gets its food from the soil?
Ruth: No. The roots absorb water and minerals. The plant makes sugars using light.
Maya held the paler leaf beside a colour card and noted its shade of green.

readingBlocks.zh: 露丝把两片落叶对着光举起。它们的绿色深浅不同。窗边示意图描述光合作用：绿色植物用光能把水和二氧化碳转成糖。根吸收水，叶从空气中吸收二氧化碳。叶绿素帮助捕获光。乔顺着箭头，从空气看到叶片，再看到小糖符号；比从头读完整标签容易理解。

readingBlocks.zh:
乔：图说叶子从土里获得食物吗？
露丝：不是。根吸收水和矿物质，植物利用光制造糖。
玛雅把较浅的叶片放在色卡旁，记录绿色的深浅。

glossary.zh: 同一种颜色的深浅变化；色调
glossary.note: a shade of green；与树荫义分开。
glossary.example: The leaves were different shades of green.

externalEvidence.definition: a quality of a given color that differs slightly from another color

glossary.zh: 植物等利用光能制造有机物的光合作用
glossary.note: 此处以绿色植物说明；过程名词。

externalEvidence.definition: synthesis of compounds with the aid of radiant energy (especially in plants)

glossary.note: absorb water / carbon dioxide；本例物质吸收，不是理解知识。
glossary.example: Roots absorb water from the soil.

glossary.note: 通常不可数；项目例句非原资料引用。
glossary.example: Leaves take in carbon dioxide from the air.
glossary.exampleZh: 叶从空气吸收二氧化碳。

externalEvidence.definition: a heavy odorless colorless gas formed during respiration and by the decomposition of organic substances; absorbed from the air by plants in photosynthesis

glossary.zh: 帮助植物捕获光的绿色色素；叶绿素
glossary.note: 不可数；不等于全部叶片结构。 WordNet的四种表述属旧资料概括，不作为现代色素总数。

externalEvidence.definition: any of a group of green pigments found in photosynthetic organisms; there are four naturally occurring forms
